title: Louisiana warns against flesh-eating bacteria after five deaths
facts: The Louisiana Department of Health issued a public warning after five people died from Vibrio vulnificus bacterial infections.
Nine cases of Vibrio vulnificus infection were confirmed in Louisiana in 2026.
Louisiana previously averaged seven Vibrio vulnificus cases and one fatality annually over the prior 10-year period.
All nine Vibrio vulnificus infections in Louisiana in 2026 involved open wounds exposed to seawater.
All individuals diagnosed with Vibrio vulnificus in Louisiana in 2026 had underlying health conditions.
Vibrio bacteria naturally inhabit coastal marine environments and multiply during warmer summer months.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention stated humans can contract Vibrio through consuming raw or undercooked shellfish.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported that approximately 1 in 5 individuals infected with Vibrio vulnificus die.
Individuals with liver disease, cancer, diabetes, HIV, or thalassemia face elevated risks from Vibrio vulnificus.
Individuals taking stomach acid-reducing medications are identified as having heightened susceptibility to Vibrio infections.
Symptoms of Vibrio vulnificus include watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, nausea, vomiting, fever, and chills.
Louisiana health officials advised seeking immediate medical care if wounds exposed to salt water show signs of swelling or discoloration.
Louisiana recorded at least 17 Vibrio vulnificus cases during the previous year.
At least 10 people died from Vibrio infections across Florida, Louisiana, and North Carolina during the previous year.
Vibrio bacteria infections can enter the human body when open cuts come into direct contact with brackish coastal waters.
